newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia outlines privatisation programme for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia outlines privatisation programme for 1997.

text.p: Tunisia said on Tuesday it would start selling off its cement industry and three hotels as part of its privatisation programme in 1997.

"Privatisation of three cement factories this year will be done by steps," Moncef Ben Abdallah, junior minister in charge of privatisation at the Economic Development Ministry, told journalists at a briefing.
"The first tender will be launched by April or May," he added.
Tunisia has six state-owned cement factories. All of them are expected to be privatised.
"We plan to sell off this year the last three hotels still owned by the state: Hilton, Africa and Sahara Palace," Ben Abdallah added.

The 500-bed five-star Hilton is located in Tunis. The Tunis 302-bed five star Hotel Africa is owned by state-controlled Societe Tunisienne de Banques. The four-star Sahara Palace is located in the oasis city of Nefta, in southern Tunisia.
The state had sold off more than 20 hotels since the 1980s. Most of them were managed by the state-controlled Societe Hoteliere Touristique de Tunisie.
The state made massive investments in tourism in the 1960s and 1970s in an attempt to persuade private investors to follow, which they did.
Ben Abdallah also said that mineral water bottler SOSTEM would also float part of its capital at the Tunis Stock Exchange but timing would depend on the market.
The state already sold to a private group a majority 51 percent stake in SOSTEM last year.
"More trade and medium size firms will also be privatised," Ben Abdallah added without elaborating.

Ben Abdallah earler said that Tunisia planned to privatise 63 public firms by the end on 1997 and that the aim by mid-year was to privatise 50 percent of the 63 firms assets estimated at $1.4 billion.

In 1996, there were 32 privatisation operations carried out, with the selling off of 19 state-owned firms. These operations included four in the transports sector, six in the industry, one in agriculture, five in the tourism and spa sectors, and three in the trade sector, he said.
In 1995, there were 15 privatisation operations, he added.
